reproduction_target: Comparative genomic reconstruction of gene-duplication dynamics and regulatory evolution across Asterales: de novo chromosome-level assembly and annotation of three new genomes (Acicarpha procumbens, Scaevola aemula, Platycodon grandiflorus) plus consistent re-annotation of five published Asterales genomes; organelle (plastid and mitochondrial) assembly and annotation; k-mer based genome characterisation (Jellyfish/GenomeScope 2.0, KMC3/Smudgeplot); duplication classification with MCScanX; orthology and species-tree inference (OrthoFinder v2.5.5, IQ-TREE v2.1.3); synteny and syntenic-depth analysis (JCVI v1.3.8); subgenome phasing with WGDI v0.6.5 and ASTRAL-III v5.7.8; reference-free Cactus v2.5.1 alignment followed by a PHAST phyloFit/phastCons/phastBias/phyloP accelerated-region scan with a custom permutation hotspot test; KS/Ka estimation (MUSCLE + PAL2NAL + codeml/PAML) with ksrates rescaling and WHALE WGD hypothesis testing; gene-family-size evolution (phytools ace, TreePL, CAFE v5.0); positive-selection testing (AlexandrusPS site models, MACSE + HyPhy aBSREL branch-site models); and BLASTP/clusterProfiler GO enrichment against TAIR10. Plant sourcing and growth, DNA/RNA extraction, Omni-C/Hi-C library preparation and all Illumina/DNBseq/PacBio/ONT sequencing are wet-lab (W, OOS for computational reproduction).
granularity_note: Coarse, one step per named tool/analysis invocation, derived from the 'Online Methods' section of the bioRxiv v2 JATS XML. WebFetch of the .source.xml returned HTTP 403; the same URL fetched with curl and a browser user-agent returned HTTP 200 (260,318 bytes) and the title phrase 'Gene duplication dynamics and regulatory evolution shape the diversification' was verified present in the fetched text, so this report is about the correct paper. The Methods section is complete and unusually detailed in the main text (18 subsections), so no supplement fetch was needed for step extraction. Stage-1 prose-only: no workflow file exists to read, env_capture_class is 'n/a' on every step and the verdict ceiling is RI. 7 wet-lab steps counted in W and not verdicted. One computational step (C11, manual Juicebox curation) is scored X rather than NI because human GUI scaffolding decisions with no published session record cannot be recovered from any artifact; its curated output IS deposited, so downstream steps are not poisoned.

steps.label: FastQC v. 0.11.9 - quality check of raw PacBio/ONT long reads and Illumina/DNBseq short reads for Acicarpha, Scaevola and Platycodon; no parameters or output thresholds stated (defaults implied)
PAUVRE v. 0.2.3 - length/quality distribution plots of raw ONT and PacBio reads (Supplementary Fig. 19); no parameters stated

fastp v. 0.23.2 - adapter removal and quality trimming of raw reads; NO trimming thresholds, quality cutoffs, length filters or flags are given anywhere ('trimmed raw reads to filter out inadequate reads and remove adapters')

guppy v. 3.1.6 (ONT python package) - base calling of Platycodon MinION data with model R9.4.1_450bps in high-accuracy mode; raw signal (fast5/pod5) is not explicitly listed as deposited, only 'raw data' under PRJNA1253301
HifiASM v. 0.19.5 (Scaevola) and v. 0.18.5 (Acicarpha) - long-read assembly with Hi-C (Scaevola) / Omni-C (Acicarpha) integration producing two haplotypes per species; no command line or flags given
MaSuRCA v. 3.4.2 - hybrid ONT long-read + DNBseq short-read assembly of Platycodon; no configuration file or parameters given
bowtie2 v. 2.1.4 + pilon v. 1.22 - short-read polishing of the Platycodon hybrid assembly; NO parameters and no number of polishing rounds stated
BWA v. 0.7.17 - alignment of Omni-C (Acicarpha) and Hi-C (Scaevola, Platycodon) reads to the draft assemblies; algorithm (mem vs aln/sampe) and all flags unstated

Samtools v1.11 - SAM to BAM conversion, coordinate sorting, and FASTA indexing of the assembly to prepare for scaffolding; sub-commands implied, no flags; input alignments are undeposited intermediates
YaHS v1.1 (Acicarpha) and v. 1.2a.2 (Platycodon, Scaevola) - Hi-C/Omni-C scaffolding; input data type per species is stated, no flags or resolution settings given

Juicer Pre tools v1.1 (bundled in YaHS) + Juicebox v. 2.17.00 (Acicarpha) / v. 2.15.00 (Scaevola, Platycodon) - MANUAL GUI scaffolding and correction to produce pseudochromosomes. The curation decisions are human GUI actions with no assembly-review log, .assembly edit file or session record published; this step cannot be re-executed from any published artifact. The curated OUTPUT is deposited (NCBI PRJNA1253301 + CoGe), so downstream steps are not poisoned
BUSCO v. 5.4.7 - assembly completeness against the embryophyta lineage from OrthoDB (orthodb.org); the OrthoDB release / lineage-dataset build date is not pinned

assemblathon_stats python script from github.com/lexnederbragt/sequencetools (blob/master path, NO version/commit) - assembly statistics of the finalised assemblies. The cited URL .../blob/master/assemblathon_stats.py returns HTTP 404; the live repo root contains assemblathon_stats.pl (Perl), i.e. the cited filename/language is wrong but an authoritative equivalent survives in the same repo (redundancy rescue)

Kraken2 v. 2.0.8 with 'StandardDB' - bacterial contaminant screening of the three new genomes; all contigs with positive hits removed. The Kraken2 Standard database is a rolling build: no build date, release or checksum is given, and no confidence/threshold parameter is stated

EDTA (Extensive de-novo TE Annotator) pipeline v. 1.9.3, which internally runs RepeatModeler2 - de novo TE library construction; 'default parameters, except --overwrite, --sensitive, --anno, and --evaluate were set to 1'

RepeatMasker v. 4.1.5 - soft-masking of the decontaminated genomes using the EDTA-derived TE library; search engine, sensitivity and other flags unstated; the TE library itself is an undeposited intermediate
Braker3 v. 3.0.3 - structural gene annotation of the soft-masked genomes using RNA-seq evidence; no protein evidence set, no GeneMark/AUGUSTUS settings, no flags given
InterProScan v. 5.66-98.0 - functional annotation of predicted proteins; member-database releases are implied by the pin but no applications/flags are listed

OMArk v. 0.3.0 (omark.omabrowser.org, accessed June 3 2024) - proteome quality assessment of Acicarpha, Scaevola and Platycodon with Asterids (NCBI taxid 71274) as the ancestral clade; the OMAmer database version is not pinned, only the access date

Re-annotation of five publicly available genomes (Nymphoides, Arctium, Chrysanthemum, Helianthus, Lactuca) by repeating the Kraken2/EDTA/RepeatMasker/Braker3/InterProScan chain 'following the steps detailed above'; source assemblies are public (PRJNA764011, PRJNA173551, PRJNA681093, HA412-HO v2, CNP0002767) and the re-annotated outputs are deposited on CoGe
gff3_stats python script from GenomeQC (github.com/HuffordLab/GenomeQC, blob/master, NO version/commit) - annotation quality statistics across all eight taxa
GetOrganelle toolkit (NO version) - chloroplast genome assembly from trimmed paired-end short reads, 'recommended parameters for embryophyte plant plastomes' plus -R 75 --disentangle-time-limit 7200
ptGAUL (NO version, NO parameters) - chloroplast sequence extraction from PacBio and ONT MinION long reads

GeSeq (NO version, NO parameters) - annotation of the complete circular plastome sequences; GeSeq is a hosted web service (chlorobox.mpimp-golm.mpg.de) whose reference-database state at run time is not recorded, and the assembled plastomes are not stated to be deposited
Mauve progressive alignment (progressiveMauve; NO version, NO parameters) - collinearity assessment between the assembled plastomes

OatK v. 1.0 (github.com/c-zhou/oatk) - mitochondrial genome assembly of Platycodon, Scaevola and Acicarpha; no parameters, no input read set specified, and the mitochondrial assemblies are not stated to be deposited
Jellyfish (NO version) k-mer counting at k = 21 followed by GenomeScope 2.0 - genome size, heterozygosity and repetitiveness estimation; Jellyfish is unversioned, so the step is unpinned overall

KMC3 (NO version) heterozygous k-mer pair extraction + Smudgeplot (NO version) ploidy inference; cutoffs described as L = (kcov/2)-5 following the Smudgeplot documentation at github.com/KamilSJaron/smudgeplot (floating main branch), but the upper cutoff U is not given numerically

MCScanX 'duplicate_gene_classifier' (NO version, NO parameters) - classification of duplicated genes as segmental, proximal, tandem or dispersed across the ten genomes; the required upstream all-vs-all BLAST step and its settings are not described

OrthoFinder v. 2.5.5 with -M msa - orthogroup inference and multiple species alignment across the ten genomes; the aligner and tree inference programs invoked under -M msa are left at defaults and not named

IQ-TREE v. 2.1.3 - model selection and maximum-likelihood species tree from the OrthoFinder alignment with 1,000 bootstraps; bootstrap type (ultrafast vs standard), partitioning and the selected model are not stated; the input alignment is an undeposited intermediate
Longest-isoform filtering of OrthoFinder orthogroups ('we filtered the groups to exclude multiple isoforms of the same gene by keeping only the longest isoform') - no tool named, no script published
JCVI v. 1.3.8 'compara catalog ortholog' with the default c-score cutoff of 0.7 - syntenic region identification among the eight Asterales genomes, plus genome-wide synteny plots
JCVI v. 1.3.8 'compara synteny depth' - pairwise syntenic gene depth between all genome pairs, used as input to subgenome phasing

WGDI v. 0.6.5 - subgenome phasing and polyploidy investigation using Vitis as reference, following the protocol at github.com/SunPengChuan/wgdi-example/blob/main/phase_subgenomes.md (floating main branch, no commit pin). SubPhaser v. (unversioned) was also attempted and abandoned as unsuitable for paleopolyploids. Vitis chromosome 11 was selected by trying multiple chromosomes and keeping the one with the largest gene retention/collinearity, and KS age estimates were used to 'help separate subgenomes' - both are analyst judgement calls that are not encoded in any published rule
WGDI '-at' parameter to generate gene trees with IQ-TREE, then ASTRAL-III v. 5.7.8 - subgenome coalescent tree; ASTRAL parameters not stated
WGDI '-r' parameter - gene fractionation assessment within each subgenome to date subgenome origin; no further settings given

JCVI re-analysis of the phased subgenomes within Asteraceae, Calyceraceae and Goodeniaceae 'using methods detailed above'; inputs are the undeposited phased-subgenome sets (partially summarised in Supplementary Datasets 1 and 2)

Cactus v2.5.1 - reference-free multiple alignment of the Asterales subgenomes syntenic to Vitis chromosome 11, using the inferred subgenome phylogeny (Supplementary Fig. 11) as the guide tree; no config file, no Cactus parameters, and the guide tree is given only as a figure

RepeatModeler + RepeatMasker on the most ancestral sequence of the subgenome alignment, then a random sample of 100,000 ancestral-repeat sites to build a MAF - RepeatModeler version not stated at this call site, the sampling is custom code with no published script and NO random seed
PHAST phyloFit (NO version) - neutral model of sequence evolution from the ancestral-repeat MAF, 'using default settings and the same phylogeny used to generate the subgenome alignment'

PHAST phastCons (NO version) - conserved-element detection within the Asterales subgenomes with Vitis as reference, run separately for the three clade analyses; log-odds scores converted to length-normalised log-odds ratios and elements below the 30th percentile excluded. The phastCons tuning parameters (--target-coverage, --expected-length, --rho) are not given
PHAST phastBias (NO version) - GC-biased gene conversion detection; regions with score > 0.5 considered gBGC-affected and removed from the conserved-element lists

PHAST phyloP (NO version) - likelihood-ratio test for accelerated evolution of conserved elements in the three clades of interest, with Storey's correction at FDR = 0.05; phyloP mode/method flags not stated
Association of accelerated regions (ARs) with genes by exon overlap using the Vitis genome annotation - no tool named (no bedtools/GenomicRanges call given), no script published

AR hotspot detection by the permutation method of Cahill et al.: sliding 100 kb windows in 10 kb steps along Vitis chromosome 11, 100 permutations randomly designating N conserved elements as accelerated, hotspot threshold at the 95th percentile of maximum simulated AR density. Custom code, NOT published, and NO random seed reported
MUSCLE (NO version, NO parameters) - protein alignment of homologous/orthologous gene pairs inside the KS pipeline
PAL2NAL (NO version, NO parameters) - conversion of the MUSCLE protein alignments to codon (nucleotide) alignments

codeml within PAML (NO version) - Ka and KS estimation between gene pairs using the F3X4 codon frequency model; the control file (.ctl) with runmode, model, cleandata and the remaining codeml settings is not given or published

R (NO version) with ggplot2 (NO version) geom_density() - kernel density estimation plots of paralog and pairwise-ortholog KS distributions; bandwidth/kernel/adjust settings not stated, plotting script not published
ksrates (NO version) - re-scaling of ortholog KS distributions to the paralog scale of each focal species, with Platycodon as outgroup; the ksrates config file is not published

WHALE (NO version) - likelihood-based WGD hypothesis testing of nine WGD events split into three analyses, 'directly following previously published methods and scripts' at gitlab.com/barker-lab/ajb_special_issue_2024.git. That repository is a PRIOR PUBLICATION's script set (McKibben et al. 2024 AJB, doi 10.1002/ajb2.16378), HTTP 200, 30 commits, 1 branch, 0 tags (no release to pin), and its README states 'All scripts are provided as is with no guarantee they will run correctly without modification on a particular operating system'. No commit hash is cited by this paper

phytools (NO version) 'ace' function with the fast ancestral-state algorithm in R (NO version) - ancestral reconstruction of orthogroup presence/absence, then six targeted orthogroup filters applied at a Bayes factor threshold of 10; the filtering script is not published

TreePL (NO version) - ultrametric calibration of the OrthoFinder phylogeny with four fossil calibration points (72.1, 47.5, 22, 31 Mya) and a 121-126 Mya secondary root constraint; optimal smoothing chosen by cross-validation over 20 values from 1e-10 to 1e+09

CAFE v. 5.0 - gene family expansion/contraction dynamics on the TreePL-calibrated tree; models varied over 1 to 3 gamma rate categories, orthogroups retained at Viterbi p <= 0.05; the CAFE input matrix and the criterion used to pick the 'best-fitting model' are not published

BLASTP (NO version) of genes from significantly expanded orthogroups against the Arabidopsis thaliana TAIR10 protein database to assign closest gene similarity, plus tree visualisation in R; TAIR10 is public but no release/download date is given and no e-value is stated for this particular search

AlexandrusPS pipeline (NO version, NO parameters) - orthology assessment and site-specific positive-selection testing on single-copy orthogroups for all taxa; the underlying model set (e.g. codeml site models / significance threshold) is not stated

Curation of 335 flowering-associated orthogroups from GO annotations of the Arabidopsis TAIR10 genome using 18 named GO terms (meristem, flower development, inflorescence, phase transition). No tool or script named; the TAIR10 GO annotation release/date is not pinned; one listed identifier is malformed ('GO:009911', 7 digits instead of 8), and the vegetative-shoot group as printed contains only four terms
MACSE (NO version) - codon alignment of coding sequences adding gaps for frameshifts and replacing stop codons with gaps; sub-program (alignSequences/refineAlignment) and cost parameters not stated

HyPhy (NO version) aBSREL - adaptive branch-site random effects likelihood test for episodic positive selection on a proportion of branches, for both the 586 site-selected orthogroups and the 335 flowering orthogroups; branch-set specification and significance threshold not stated; results inspected in HyPhy Vision (hosted service, vision.hyphy.org/aBSREL)
Gene-tree visualisation in R using Ape 5.0 (version pinned) and ggtree (NO version); no plotting script published

clusterProfiler (NO version) in R (NO version) - GO biological-process enrichment of expanded/contracted and positively selected gene sets, annotated by BLASTP best-hit matches to TAIR10 at e-value 1e-10, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction, significance at adjusted p < 0.01; the enrichment universe/background set is not defined and the script is not published

Taxon and material sourcing: Acicarpha procumbens seeds collected in Uruguay, Platycodon grandiflorus 'Komachi' seeds purchased from Park Seed, Scaevola aemula cuttings from North Carolina Farms Inc.; greenhouse growth at University of Memphis and Auburn University; one Platycodon individual inbred for two generations; vouchers deposited at MEM and AUA herbaria (Supplementary Table 7)
Genomic DNA extraction: E.Z.N.A. SP Plant DNA Kit from ~25 mg fresh leaf (Acicarpha, Scaevola) and a modified CTAB protocol from ~100 mg homogenised tissue (Platycodon); Bead Mill 24 Homogenizer

High molecular weight DNA isolation: TaKaRa NucleoBond HMW DNA kit from 2.5-3 g flash-frozen leaf (Acicarpha, Scaevola); ONT CTAB-Genomic-tip protocol with Amicon Ultra purification and Circulomics Short Read Eliminator v2 size selection (Platycodon)

RNA extraction from young leaf, shoot apical meristem and mature leaf tissues with the E.Z.N.A. Plant RNA kit (#R6827-01) and RNase-free DNase (#E1091), plus KAPA stranded mRNA-seq library preparation at UNC HTSF
Chromatin conformation library preparation: Dovetail Omni-C kit (Acicarpha, at HudsonAlpha) and Phase Genomics Proximo Hi-C Kit-Plant #KT3040 v4.0 protocol, October 2020 (Scaevola, Platycodon)

Short-read sequencing: Illumina NovaSeq 6000 PE150 (Acicarpha, Scaevola gDNA and RNA), NovaSeq PE-50/PE-100 (Scaevola Hi-C), KAPA Hyper DNA libraries on BGI DNBseq PE100 (Platycodon gDNA), NovaSeq 6000 PE100 (Platycodon Hi-C)

Long-read sequencing: PacBio Sequel II (Acicarpha, Scaevola HMW DNA, at HudsonAlpha); ONT Ligation Sequencing Kit SQK-LSK109 on a MinION Mk1B (MIN-101B) with FLO-MIN106D R9.4.1 flow cells under MinKNOW v3.6.5, two flow cells each washed three times with EXP-WSH003 and reloaded (Platycodon)

headline.static_readiness: 0/62 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification). Unexecuted; declared environment statically valid but not verified as the env that produced the results. n_exact_capture_unexecuted = 0, n_fetch_required = 0. This zero under-claims by construction: Tier-1 cannot credit an undeclared-but-present dependency.
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: RI ceiling on 25/62 computational steps (40%). Those are the steps where all four axes reach at least 1, which here means an exact version pin is present in prose: FastQC 0.11.9, PAUVRE 0.2.3, guppy 3.1.6, HifiASM 0.19.5/0.18.5, MaSuRCA 3.4.2, Samtools 1.11, YaHS 1.1/1.2a.2, BUSCO 5.4.7, Kraken2 2.0.8, EDTA 1.9.3, RepeatMasker 4.1.5, Braker3 3.0.3, InterProScan 5.66-98.0, OMArk 0.3.0, OrthoFinder 2.5.5, IQ-TREE 2.1.3, JCVI 1.3.8, WGDI 0.6.5, ASTRAL-III 5.7.8, Cactus 2.5.1 and CAFE 5.0. Every one of those pins is a scattered prose '==' pin with no interpreter, channel or platform declaration, so version is capped at 1 (exact_pins_partial) and no step can exceed RI even at Stage 2 on environment grounds. 36/62 steps (58%) cap at NI, driven by two causes: (a) no version stated at all for a large second tier of tools (GetOrganelle, ptGAUL, GeSeq, Mauve, Jellyfish, KMC3, Smudgeplot, MCScanX, PHAST phyloFit/phastCons/phastBias/phyloP, MUSCLE, PAL2NAL, PAML codeml, ksrates, WHALE, phytools, TreePL, BLAST, AlexandrusPS, MACSE, HyPhy, ggtree, clusterProfiler, R itself), and (b) three steps (C3 fastp, C7 bowtie2+pilon, C8 BWA, C23 ptGAUL, C24 GeSeq, C26 OatK, C47 MUSCLE, C48 PAL2NAL, C57 AlexandrusPS, C61 Ape/ggtree) state no parameters whatsoever. 1/62 step is X (C11, unrecorded manual Juicebox curation). The paper deposits no analysis code of its own, so the Code axis never exceeds 1 anywhere.
headline.coverage: 62 computational steps assessed from the main-text Online Methods prose; 7 wet-lab/physical steps (material sourcing and vouchering, gDNA extraction, HMW DNA isolation, RNA extraction and mRNA library prep, Omni-C/Hi-C library prep, short-read sequencing, long-read sequencing) counted in W and out of computational-reproduction scope. Computational coverage = 62/69 (90%).

gaps.where: Whole paper - there is NO Code availability statement anywhere (main text, back matter, or landing page)
gaps.missing: No repository of this study's own analysis code is deposited or linked. The back matter contains Acknowledgements, Author contributions, Data availability and Funding, and nothing else. Every one of the 62 computational steps therefore has Code <= 1 (reconstructable from prose at best). The five non-tool-homepage URLs in the Methods are all third-party: github.com/lexnederbragt/sequencetools (assembly stats, cited path 404), github.com/HuffordLab/GenomeQC (gff3_stats), github.com/SunPengChuan/wgdi-example (a how-to document, floating main branch), github.com/KamilSJaron/smudgeplot (tool docs), and gitlab.com/barker-lab/ajb_special_issue_2024 which is a PRIOR PUBLICATION's script set (McKibben et al. 2024 AJB). Substantial custom logic is unpublished: the ancestral-repeat sampling, the 30th-percentile log-odds filter, the AR-to-exon association, the AR hotspot permutation test, the longest-isoform orthogroup filter, the Bayes-factor-10 orthogroup classification, the CAFE input construction, the GO-term-based flowering orthogroup curation, and every figure-generation script.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the full analysis codebase (assembly/annotation driver scripts, the PHAST accelerated-region pipeline, the permutation hotspot test, the KS pipeline wrapper, the CAFE and selection-analysis drivers, and all figure scripts) in a public repository with a tagged release and a Zenodo DOI, and add a Code availability statement to the main text.

gaps.where: Environment closure across the whole paper (all 62 computational steps)
gaps.missing: No environment lock of any kind is claimed: no conda-lock/pixi.lock/renv.lock, no environment.yml, no requirements.txt, no container image or digest, no interpreter version (Python and R are both used but neither is versioned), no channel or platform declaration. What exists is scattered prose '==' style pins for roughly one third of the named tools. Under the rubric's symmetric env-closure gate this is version=1, subtier exact_pins_partial, for every pinned step; no step can reach R-star on environment grounds even at Stage 2.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a conda-lock (or pixi.lock / container digest) covering the interpreter, channels and declared platform for the full assembly-to-selection stack, alongside the analysis code.

gaps.where: 36 of 62 computational steps - no version stated at all
gaps.missing: No version is given for GetOrganelle, ptGAUL, GeSeq, progressiveMauve, Jellyfish, KMC3, Smudgeplot, MCScanX, RepeatModeler (at the ancestral-repeat call site), PHAST (phyloFit, phastCons, phastBias, phyloP), MUSCLE, PAL2NAL, PAML/codeml, ksrates, WHALE, phytools, TreePL, BLAST/BLASTP, AlexandrusPS, MACSE, HyPhy, ggtree, clusterProfiler, SubPhaser, the assemblathon_stats and gff3_stats scripts, or R itself. Note the internal inconsistency: the paper is meticulous about pinning assembly-stage tools (FastQC through Cactus) and almost entirely silent about versions for the downstream evolutionary-analysis stage, which is where the paper's actual claims are made.
gaps.how_to_close: Add a software-versions supplementary table naming and pinning every tool, interpreter, R package and Python library actually used, including the downstream analysis stack.

gaps.where: C11 (manual Juicebox curation), C40 (ancestral-repeat sampling), C42 (30th-percentile filter), C45 (AR-exon association), C46 (AR hotspot permutation), C32 (longest-isoform filter), C53 (Bayes-factor-10 orthogroup classification), C58 (flowering orthogroup curation), C50/C61 (all R plotting)
gaps.missing: Nine custom procedures are described in prose but implemented by unpublished code or by unrecorded human action. C11 is the most severe: Hi-C scaffolding was finished by manual correction in the Juicebox GUI with no published .assembly/.review file or edit log, so the step itself is unreproducible (scored X). C46's permutation test and C40's random 100,000-site sample are stochastic with NO reported seed. The threshold logic (30th percentile of length-normalised log-odds, gBGC score > 0.5, Bayes factor 10, Viterbi <= 0.05, 95th percentile of maximum simulated density) is stated precisely, which is why these steps are recoverable in principle - but the implementations are absent.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the scripts together with the intermediate inputs they consume; export and deposit the Juicebox assembly-review file so the curation can be replayed; record and report the RNG seeds for the permutation and sampling steps.

gaps.where: External reference resources consumed by C12 (BUSCO/OrthoDB), C14 (Kraken2 StandardDB), C18 (InterProScan member DBs), C19 (OMArk/OMAmer), C24 (GeSeq reference set), C56/C58/C62 (TAIR10 protein and GO annotations), C33-C39 (Vitis reference genome and annotation)
gaps.missing: Every external database is named but not pinned by release, build date or checksum, and none is fetched by any published rule. The Kraken2 'StandardDB' is a rolling build whose composition changes weekly and materially determines which contigs were removed as contaminants. The BUSCO embryophyta lineage dataset from OrthoDB has no release. TAIR10 is named as a stable release but no download date or file version is given for either the protein FASTA or the GO annotation. OMArk gets an access date (June 3, 2024) but no OMAmer database version. Because Stage 1 forbids A/B/C assignment without a code check, env_capture_class is 'n/a' everywhere; at Stage 2 these would be Class B at best and the Kraken2 Standard DB would likely be Class C (mutable-fetch-fatal).
gaps.how_to_close: State the exact release/build of every database (Kraken2 DB build date and md5, OrthoDB release, InterProScan member-DB versions, OMAmer database version, TAIR10 file names with download dates) and fetch each one in a versioned download rule inside the published workflow.

gaps.missing: The cited URL https://github.com/lexnederbragt/sequencetools/blob/master/assemblathon_stats.py returns HTTP 404. The repository itself is live (HTTP 200) but its root contains assemblathon_stats.pl (Perl), not a .py file, so the paper cites both the wrong filename and the wrong language. This is a redundancy-rescue case: an authoritative equivalent survives in the same repository, so the step is not scored as lost, but a reader following the citation literally hits a dead link. The same repository is referenced by floating 'master' with no commit, as is the GenomeQC gff3_stats script (C21) and the wgdi-example protocol document (C35).
gaps.how_to_close: Cite the correct file (assemblathon_stats.pl) at a pinned commit or tag, or vendor the script into the paper's own deposited repository.

gaps.missing: The entire WGD hypothesis-testing sub-pipeline is externalised to a prior publication's script set at gitlab.com/barker-lab/ajb_special_issue_2024 ('Directly following previously published methods and scripts'). That repository is live (HTTP 200) with 30 commits, 1 branch and 0 tags, so there is no release to pin and this paper cites no commit hash. Its README explicitly disclaims runnability: 'All scripts are provided as is with no guarantee they will run correctly without modification on a particular operating system.' The nine tested WGD events are enumerated only by reference to Supplementary Fig. 15, and no WHALE configuration is given.
gaps.how_to_close: Vendor the exact scripts used (or cite a tagged release / commit hash of the upstream repository) and publish the WHALE configuration and input gene-tree sets for each of the three analyses.

gaps.where: C40 (random 100,000-site ancestral-repeat sample), C46 (100-permutation AR hotspot test), and implicitly C31 (IQ-TREE 1,000 bootstraps) and C55 (CAFE model fitting)
gaps.missing: No RNG seeds are reported anywhere in the paper. The permutation count (100), window geometry (100 kb / 10 kb) and percentile threshold (95th) are fully specified for the hotspot test, and the sample size (100,000 sites) is specified for the neutral-model sample, so results should agree distributionally; exact reproduction of the published hotspot list is not possible from the description. IQ-TREE bootstrap replicates and the CAFE optimiser are likewise seedless.
gaps.how_to_close: Record seeds in the published scripts, or state explicitly that only distributional agreement is expected and deposit the realised permutation outputs and the AR/hotspot tables.

gaps.missing: Two steps depend on hosted web services whose state at run time is not recorded, which is the closest analogue in the 13-type dictionary to a proprietary/uncontrolled dependency: GeSeq (chlorobox.mpimp-golm.mpg.de) performed the plastome annotation, and results were inspected through HyPhy Vision (vision.hyphy.org/aBSREL). Neither service version nor its reference-database state is given, and no submission parameters or job identifiers are reported. OMArk (omark.omabrowser.org) is borderline but is at least given a version (0.3.0) and an access date (June 3, 2024). Note the dictionary has no hosted-service type; recorded as 11 with this qualification rather than silently dropped.
